_about: Semantic slot -> shape id on the exemplar deck (wfo-sales-deck.pptx, 10 slides, 13.33 x 7.5 in). `ref` is the 1-based slide number in the exemplar; ids are p:cNvPr ids, stable for this file. build_deck_v2.py reads this map and never hard-codes geometry. Ambiguous shapes and the reasoning behind each resolution are documented in references/exemplar-builder.md.

header.note: placeholder idx=34 on every content slide (2-10); absent on the cover

cover.note: The dark ground and the hero photo come from the Title-AI LAYOUT, not from slide shapes. Shape 3 is one placeholder holding BOTH the pack name (p0, 44 pt) and the one-liner (p1, 25 pt). Shape 2 carries the reference's tier ladder; the builder empties that text (no tier eyebrow, DECK-FIDELITY finding 2) and reuses the shape for the ICP line. `cover.photo` is the Workforce Optimization hero image on the layout — pack-specific, so it is replaced from `deck.images.cover` or removed, never inherited; the layout's own ink background (`solidFill tx1`) is the empty state.

use_case.note: Shape 9 paragraphs: p0 lead (bold clause + regular tail), p1 blank, p2 'This leads to the following challenges:', p3-p5 the bulleted named challenges (bold label + ': rest'). p3 is the bullet prototype. Shape 13: p0 bold reframe + regular body, p1 blank, p2 the second sentence.

verticals.note: Four identical 6.00 x 2.00 in cards. `icon` is a 1.06 in white PNG centred on the blue `panel`; the builder replaces it in place from assets/icons/map.yaml, or leaves the exemplar's icon and says so. `card`/`panel` are greyed for an unused slot (rule 3: empty container, never a gap).

today_tomorrow.note: Shape 17 is the source customer's logo — removed unless clearance allows the customer name AND deck.images.customer_logo is given; the headline then moves to the left margin and widens to the content band (the only geometry the builder computes on this slide). TOMORROW's band is orange here, not blue: the exemplar's own choice, kept.

proof.note: Four quadrant blocks: [0] CONTEXT and [1] SOLUTION carry blue bars, [2] VALUE FOR ORACLE + NVIDIA and [3] VALUE FOR CLIENT carry ink bars. The deck keeps [0] and [1] here; blocks [2]/[3] are the composition the 'why it sells' slide is duplicated from.

why_it_sells.note: The anatomy's slide 6 has no reference slide of its own: on the reference it was the 'VALUE FOR ORACLE + NVIDIA' quadrant of slide 5. The builder duplicates slide 5, drops the stat strip and the customer logo, and fills the four quadrant blocks with packages.why_it_sells_for_the_partner (ink bars first, so the partner-value colour leads).

layers.note: Row 0 is the top of the ladder and carries the two white sub-cards (the pack / the tailored solution) plus one chip per tier; it has no summary textbox or vendor badge. Rows 1..n are the plain layer rows and row 1 is the clone prototype when the spec has more than three layers. The ladder band (top of row 0 to the bottom of the last row, 2.85 -> 6.71 in) and the 0.16 in gap are the exemplar's; row heights are distributed inside it.

architecture.note: Rebuilt inside the exemplar's frame. Shape 36 ('Additional datasources') is the node prototype — a plain rounded rectangle with a centred bold name over a small description, easier to clone than the equivalent group 33, which the builder deletes. Shape 32 is a group whose child 13 holds the engine text. 19 is a 0.012 in white bar left over from the reference's own editing; it renders as nothing and is deleted.

packages.note: 11 x 4 in the exemplar: header, package scope, services price, infrastructure price, timing, then six capability rows. Row 5 is the capability prototype; its cells carry the glyph runs the builder reuses (partial 11 pt, included/advanced 18 pt orange, 'not in this tier' an em dash in C2C7CC at 12 pt) — the glyph type never comes from code.

packages_detailed.note: 8 x 4: header, scope line, six capability rows whose cells are '<glyph>  <prose>' in one paragraph — the glyph is run 0 (16 pt) and the prose the last run (9 pt). Row 2 is the prototype.

dropped.why: The reference carries three drafts of the same package table (8 without the infrastructure row, 9 with it, 10 in prose). A deck ships one table: 9 and 10 are kept, 8 is dropped.
